root_cause.text: The RDMA core's DMAH allocation handler does not validate the user-supplied cpu_id against nr_cpu_ids before passing it to cpumask_test_cpu(), causing an out-of-bounds read on the cpumask bitmap.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (dmah->cpu_id >= nr_cpu_ids) { ret = -EINVAL; goto err; }` before the call to `cpumask_test_cpu(dmah->cpu_id, current->cpus_ptr)`. The CVE description confirms that the cpu_id is passed directly to cpumask_test_cpu() without validation, leading to out-of-bounds access and a potential WARN_ON_ONCE.

This error check does not include any validation of cpu_id before the code reaches the vulnerable cpumask_test_cpu call. It is part of the control flow that fails to enforce bounds on cpu_id, allowing an invalid value to propagate.
